blocks.text: DSPM continuously scans your cloud resources against the policies enabled in your cloud accounts to identify vulnerabilities and generate alerts. When a policy violation is detected, DSPM generates alerts and sends notifications to recipients to take action and prevent any potential breaches.

An alert is an outcome of a policy evaluation done on a resource type (e.g., S3 bucket, database). For example, If a security policy is enabled to detect any publicly exposed S3 bucket containing sensitive data, and there are 5 such S3 buckets in your cloud storage, DSPM generates 5 alerts.
Alerts are categorized by severity level to help you prioritize them and take action in a timely manner.
Alerts provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: View and manage alert notifications for any security policy violations detected in the cloud accounts.
Notify recipients to take action and prevent any potential breaches.
Stay informed about critical security events.

On the Alerts page (Data Security > DSPM > Alerts), you can see the following tabs:

blocks.item: Grouped By Policy
You can view the policies for which alerts are generated. To learn more, see Viewing Alerts Grouped by Policy.
Grouped By Resource
You can view the resources for which alerts are generated. To learn more, see Viewing Alerts Grouped by Resource.
All Alerts
On the All Alerts tab, you can do the following:
Apply filters to view specific data.
By default, alerts with an open status are displayed.
Add additional filters.
Customize the page settings.
Search for specific data in the searchable column. You can also export the search results with the applied filters and download the report as an Excel file.
Export the data and download the report as an Excel file.
Show or hide columns in the table.
View the list of alerts generated for policy violations. For each alert, you can view:
Alert ID: The unique identifier for the alert. Click to view additional details.
Resource Name: The name of the resource.
Policy Name: The policy title.
Policy Category: The threat category (Public Exposure, Data Loss, etc.) to which the policy belongs.
Resource Type: The type of data store (AWS EC2 instance, AWS S3 bucket, etc.).
Resource ID: The unique identifier for the resource.
Risk Level: The risk level (Critical, High, Medium, or Low) of the alert.

The risk level of an alert is calculated as the average of the policy severity and the resource impact. For example, if the policy severity is Critical and the resource impact is Medium, then the alert risk level is High.
Alert Status: The status (Open, Closed, Resolved, and Snoozed) of the alert.
Cloud Account: The unique identifier of the cloud account (AWS, Azure, GCP, Snowflake, and On-Premises) in which the resource is located.
Created Date: The date and time the alert was generated.
Last Updated: The date and time the alert was last updated.
Select one or multiple alerts to resolve, snooze, unsnooze, or reset them.
See image.
Select any of the following actions:
Resolve: Resolve an alert.
Snooze: Snooze an alert.
Unsnooze: Unsnooze the alert. This option is available only when the alert is snoozed.
Reset: Reset the alert. This option is available only when the alert is resolved.
